perspectives.title: Authors Reject AI

representative_posts.author: shannonfsmith.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Authors can read. However, is there any nuisance to their stance on AI, or is it just "AI BAD" and therefore its ethical use doesn't exist?

representative_posts.author: oliviaatwater.com
representative_posts.text: Their stance is word salad that means whatever they want it to mean at any given time. But for the record, I am an "AI BAD" author with zero nuance, especially because I once worked for a proto-AI company and I understand it extremely well. It is, in fact... just bad. And also bad at what it does.

representative_posts.author: surcomplicated.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm not joking. They are deadly serious about authors being able to opt out of any form of AI scrutiny and get very evasive the moment you press them about even goddamn antispam without actually retreating in any substantive way.

representative_posts.author: oliviaatwater.com
representative_posts.text: Machine learning is another matter, but frankly, most authors will rarely if ever interact with real machine learning in a way that matters. Everyone knows what generative AI is, and obscuring the issue with "but this completely different thing that has nothing to do with gen-AI" is taking the piss.

Authors' opposition to AI scrutiny is evasive
Most authors do not interact with machine learning in a meaningful way

representative_posts.author: mattwinkelman.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think about this a lot from the flip side. The postseason has the concentrate amount of pitching of the entire season and is obscene, but also it is what is required to keep hitting in check. The circle of trust for postseason pitching is tiny and shrinking constantly to try and stay ahead.

representative_posts.author: kilagreene.myatproto.social
representative_posts.text: Also, this is just kinda how baseball works? The best team in the regular season rarely goes on to win the World Series. It’s happened 8 times in the past 32 years and one of those was the fluke COVID season.

representative_posts.author: tomisphere.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Is your MLB team's fan base clamoring for more power bats? Have them note that the 3 teams that have gone the farthest in the playoffs this year all finished the regular season in the bottom 20% in Isolated Power. However 2 of them are top 8 in the all-important OPS, thanks to very high OBP's.

representative_posts.author: hahnapaulooza.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: They limped to the finish line (no wonder after two extended seasons, both which involved international trips to Asia). They still racked up 100 wins.
